title: PointHeartFiniteStageTruncations
statement: Fix D, l different from the characteristic, and an algebraic closure Omega of Q_l. There is a family c, over every finite-dimensional coefficient field E over Q_l in the scheme universe, of canonical upper and lower truncation comparisons for zlPointAmbient at every integer. Each comparison satisfies its prescribed counit or unit equation, and the family satisfies ZlPointScalarTruncationSquare for every finite coefficient extension E to L. The common-stage realization zlPointCommonAmbient likewise has a ZlPointTruncationComparison for the recorded common-stage standard t-structure. All specified functors and structures are those of [def-zl-point-heart-finite-stage-data].

source.place: Paragraph 7, dimension-zero input; steps 1, 2, 4 of lem-zl-point-heart-finite-stage

proof.text: First work at a finite coefficient field $E$. The source standard halves are the isomorphism closures of the integral halves. Sections on $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ are exact and satisfy $H^r\Gamma(s,K)=\Gamma(s,\mathcal H^rK)$. Rationalization of module complexes is exact: tensoring with $E=\mathcal O_E[1/\varpi_E]$ is module localization (the identification sends $x\otimes a/\varpi_E^n$ to $ax/\varpi_E^n$), and localization preserves exact sequences. Thus the specified $\operatorname{Fib}_{s,E}(K)=\Gamma(s,K)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$ preserves both standard halves. The standard module truncations preserve bounded finite-dimensional cohomology, so restrict to $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$. Both categories consequently have bounded standard t-structures. The specified fibre functor is an exact equivalence by the point-fibre theorem.

source.place: Tag 0118, section-truncations; source standard pairs and specified sections functor as cited

proof.text: Apply the t-exact truncation-comparison theorem to this exact functor: $\operatorname{Fib}_{s,E}\tau^{\le m}\cong\tau^{\le m}\operatorname{Fib}_{s,E}$ and likewise for $\tau^{\ge m}$, preserving their canonical maps. It also reflects the halves. Indeed, if its value on $K$ is in degree $\le0$, the value on $\tau^{\ge1}K$ is zero; full faithfulness reflects zero objects, since $\operatorname{id}_X=0$ whenever its image is zero. Hence $\tau^{\ge1}K=0$, which is the source degree-$\le0$ criterion. Use $\tau^{\le-1}$ for the other half. For any target heart object choose a preimage under the derived equivalence; these two arguments put that preimage in the source heart. Restricting the full-faithfulness bijections therefore gives an equivalence of these two hearts.

source.place: 1.3.3–1.3.6, canonical truncations and their universal properties; reflection argument written here

proof.text: For $E\subset L$, take the rational form of the specified sections/scalar isomorphism and then its degree-zero cohomology. Compose with the inverse of the cohomology/scalar isomorphism $[x]\otimes\lambda\mapsto[x\otimes\lambda]$. This gives $\omega_L(M\otimes_E L)\cong\omega_E(M)\otimes_E L$. The sections isomorphisms satisfy the stated identity and tower equations, and the cohomology isomorphisms satisfy their stated tower square. Their composites therefore have those same equations. Scalar extension on the source commutes with truncations by constructible truncation stability. Uniqueness of the truncation comparisons, including their naturality for transformations and their composition law, makes the square between these scalar comparisons and the comparisons in steps 2–3 commute. For $L=E$, the sections normalization and the formula on classes give the identity. At $\Omega$, the cohomology and fibre definitions use these very stage comparisons, so the same equations persist there.
